speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Deputy Speaker, I would like to declare my interest as the Executive Director of the Singapore Chinese Orchestra.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: As an active sportsman, I strongly believe in the importance of a healthy and happy lifestyle.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: However, I believe that this is not just about the body, but also the heart and soul.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: That is why the arts are so important, especially the traditional arts, which connect us to who we are today.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: More can be done to make the traditional arts an integral part of our society, bringing together people of different races, religions, and backgrounds, and creating a shared understanding across our various communities.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: We need to develop policies to strengthen the arts ecosystem so that it will be more vibrant and sustainable.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: To deepen understanding and appreciation of the traditional arts, we need to take these art forms seriously.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: We could, for example, have think-tanks to engage in research that will provide strong and sound evidence for the importance of the traditional arts.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: In addition to traditional arts, the arts-for-all can play in serving underserved and disadvantaged communities, and how more can be done to help the next generation of Singaporeans to love arts and fulfilled lives.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: I hope that the Ministry will consider issuing a "Culture Pass" via a mobile application which offers a credit similar to ActiveSG for students and senior citizens to spend on cultural events and encourage cultural discovery.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Looking to the future, we really hope to see the arts become a part of everyone’s everyday life, actively transforming the well-being of individuals, but also bringing people together as a nation and uplifting our spirits.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: For this to happen, we need alignment of all Government Ministries in supporting the arts in their policies.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: The arts and culture should become a strategic tool for Government agencies, from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) to the Ministry of Education (MOE).

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: We also need to have more physical infrastructure for arts and culture.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: The “hardware” is important if we are to grow our "heartware".

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: People need spaces to meet, exchange ideas, build a sense of community and home.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: These spaces are also where artists and the general public can interact with one another more freely.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: (In Mandarin):   Deputy Speaker, for the past many years, we have been continuously strengthening and promoting arts and culture.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: However, in order to create more exciting, colourful and diversified art platforms, more efforts are needed in the area of traditional arts.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: More can be done to make the traditional arts an integral part of our society, bringing together people of different races, religions and backgrounds, and creating a shared understanding across our various communities.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Traditional arts can best embody our roots and beliefs.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: In this regard, I have three visions and two wishes.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: The first vision is to make Singapore into a modern metropolis with unique and diversified cultural scenes, nourishing and inspiring its citizens with arts; the second vision is to make arts into a bonding agent between different communities; the third vision is for Singapore's soft power to wield international influence.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: My first wish is to recognise our veteran artists and cultivate mentors and role models to guide younger artists.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: My second wish is to develop policies to strengthen the arts ecosystem so that it will be more vibrant and sustainable.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: This is a worrying trend faced by the artists, the National Arts Council (NAC) and the Government.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: In terms of the Government, various Government Ministries should reach consensus and introduce policies to support the arts.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: The arts and culture should become a strategic tool for Government agencies, from MFA to MOE.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: We also need to have more physical infrastructure for arts and culture.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: The “hardware” is important if we are to grow our "heartware".

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: People need spaces to meet, exchange ideas, build a sense of community and home.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: These spaces are also where artists and the general public can interact with one another more freely.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Our biggest challenge is how to change people’s pragmatic mindset and increase their interest in arts and culture, making it an integral part of their life.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: We need more examples of deeper, interesting and inspiring stories to increase the influence of arts and culture.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: We need to constantly strengthen and broaden the ecosystem for the arts and culture, so that more Singaporeans can participate in arts and cultural activities, as audience, a learner or a volunteer.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: It also provides learning and career development opportunities.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: This is a very targeted assistance which I fully support.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: As our new arts roadmap goes into the next five years, I hope the Government, businesses and the people sector can strengthen their collaboration, in order to connect and absorb our diversified cultures, create a more open and richer cultural environment, and make more funds and resources available for artists.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Meanwhile, I would like to suggest that a think-tank be set up to engage in research in traditional arts and help improve our understanding and appreciation of traditional arts.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: When encouraging people to participate in traditional arts, we should also include the vulnerable groups.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: In the sports field, we have already recognised the disabled talents and given them opportunities to use their potentials.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: In the field of arts and culture, we can create more platforms for the vulnerable groups to participate and learn.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Arts must go into the masses in order to sustain vitality.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: This will generate interest and instil in their heart a passion for arts and music.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: I hope that MOE can consider making good use of the time released from doing away with examinations and shake up our arts education.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Arts education should be incorporated into our civic education.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: I hope arts and culture can be used as a vehicle to inspire creativity and innovation among our young and to reflect our national spirit.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Cultural diversity is our unique character and can resonate with Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Arts play an active role in deepening the national identity, trust among people and mutual respect among communities.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: When creating an image of a cultural metropolis, we can learn from other major cities by managing our culture and arts causes with the spirit of professionalism, through forming alliances and cultivating brand names.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: To promote arts, works of art must combine ideological elements, artistic qualities and watchability together.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: To become a cultural capital, Singapore can adopt a strategy by incorporating arts education into its school curriculum and creating a strong arts and cultural atmosphere in the society.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: I am confident that if we can incorporate our diversified culture and arts into daily lives, Singapore will become a more vibrant, attractive and cohesive place!

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: It will be a home with tenderness, warmth and elegance!

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) agrees that a vibrant and sustainable arts and culture scene brings diverse communities together, adds to our overall well-being, and roots us as a people and a nation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our cultural offerings can also inspire us and show the world who we are and what we stand for and deepen our sense of national identity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our arts and culture play a critical role in MCCY's efforts to foster a more caring, cohesive and confident Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: MCCY, NAC and the National Heritage Board (NHB) partner the public, private and people sectors to make arts and culture an integral part of the lives of all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We support and facilitate our arts community's instrumental role in developing a flourishing arts ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: More people now enjoy, appreciate and benefit from varied and diverse arts and culture programmes since we expanded access and grew these offerings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This is the highest on record since 2005, not including the peak in 2015 when there was a surge in events to celebrate SG50.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Moreover, three in four respondents said that the arts and culture improved the quality of life for everyone and agreed that our arts and culture are something that Singaporeans can be proud of.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Terence Ho noted that ticketed attendances had fallen from 2012 to 2016.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: However, that year, there were more non-ticketed performing arts activities than ever before, with attendances also the highest on record since 2012.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: MCCY and NAC are working on increasing both ticketed and non-ticketed attendance, as both types of events contribute to the vibrancy and sustainability of our arts and culture landscape.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We hope that non-ticketed arts activities will create accessible entry points to the arts, while artists and arts groups will build on the increased awareness, and create works that could interest and attract more people to become paying audience.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I agree with Mr Terence Ho that recognition of our arts practitioners helps develop role models.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Notable artistic achievement and significant contributions to the community are also recognised through National Day Awards.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: MCCY and NAC hope that award recipients will continue to give back to the community through education and mentorship, create works that resonate with both local and international audiences and inspire us through the pursuit of excellence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Plan was developed in close consultation with the arts community and seeks to make Singapore "home to diverse and distinctive arts that inspire our people, connect our communities and position Singapore globally".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NAC has identified eight priorities where it will work with our arts practitioners to achieve our shared objectives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I will elaborate more on the areas of growing audiences, building capabilities, strengthening research, and taking our arts beyond our shores, which are relevant to the points that Mr Terence Ho has raised.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Strategies for sustained audience development must cater to different groups of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I, therefore, agree with Mr Terence Ho on the importance of providing Singaporeans of all ages and backgrounds with greater access to our arts and culture.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Singaporeans already enjoy a year-round calendar of diverse cultural offerings, including exhibitions, performances and activities, as well as free access to our national museums and heritage institutions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These include popular events like our annual Singapore Art Week, Singapore Heritage Festival, PAssionArts Festival, and Singapore Night Festival.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: MCCY and NAC also partner organisations, such as the National Library Board and People's Association, to bring quality programmes directly to neighbourhood libraries, community clubs and other community spaces.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In addition, NAC brings together thought leaders, stakeholders and practitioners at platforms, such as the Arts in Eldercare Seminar and Arts and Disability Forum, to discuss how different communities can be better engaged through the arts and culture.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NAC will continue to strengthen partnerships with the social service and healthcare sectors to implement innovative programmes that can best benefit under-reached communities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Beyond programmes, the Government has invested significantly in new cultural infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The year 2015 alone saw the opening of the National Gallery Singapore and the Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We are currently revamping the Singapore Art Museum and developing a new waterfront theatre at the Esplanade.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our aspiration is for these spaces to foster audience growth, provide opportunities for interaction and inspire our people through the presentation of homegrown, Southeast Asian and international works.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As we continue our investment into infrastructural developments and platforms to showcase artistic works, we look to the arts community to create quality content which can engage new and existing audiences.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In this context, I thank Mr Terence Ho for his suggestion of a "Culture Pass” mobile application.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: MCCY and NAC will consider this as part of ongoing efforts to grow audiences and enhance the accessibility of our arts and culture, by leveraging technology.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Terence Ho rightly highlighted the importance of arts education.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Under Our SG Arts Plan, we continue to prioritise arts education efforts to nurture audiences of the future.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Early exposure to the arts fosters creative thinking and imagination, helps our children develop empathy and confidence, and makes art appreciation and participation a way of life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Arts education also helps our youths better appreciate Singapore’s cultural heritage and develop a stronger sense of national identity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: MCCY and NAC will continue to work with MOE to incorporate the arts into other learning areas, and with the arts community to create content that will inspire and develop our young minds.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Terence Ho highlighted the importance of deepening understanding, appreciation and promotion of the traditional arts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I agree that the traditional arts help tell our Singapore story, bring people from different backgrounds together, and enhance mutual understanding among different communities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: SAC complements NAC’s existing work with traditional arts groups to add to the vibrancy of districts, such as our historic Kampong Glam, and introduce more audiences to the traditional arts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: With such support, we hope that traditional arts groups will develop the skills and capabilities to present even more engaging offerings for all audiences.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In addition, NAC will partner institutions, such as the Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre, to research the development of traditional practices and forms in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This will help spur innovation and creativity and encourage greater appreciation and critical discourse.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NAC will work with NHB to explore other areas of research in the traditional arts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In addition, NAC will engage MOE and ECDA to develop interest in the traditional arts from a young age.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: (In English): Mr Terence Ho noted that our arts and culture is one way we can showcase Singapore internationally.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will support our artists to grow and scale new heights and help profile Singapore overseas.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Government will do our best and find new and better ways to provide resources, infrastructure and platforms.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I look forward to our arts community doing its part to develop diverse, rich and engaging works that can connect with and inspire audience groups across different backgrounds, including the under-served, whether arts enthusiasts or novices, at home or abroad.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Let us work together to achieve our shared vision for the arts and culture in Singapore.
